annotation.title_clean: Robot-First Mars Settlement: A Conceptual Framework for Technology Governance, Risk Reduction, and Interplanetary Policy
annotation.title_en: Robot-First Mars Settlement: A Conceptual Framework for Technology Governance, Risk Reduction, and Interplanetary Policy
annotation.venue: Innovation Journal of Social Sciences and Economic Review
annotation.summary_en: Conceptual journal article proposing a robot-first Mars settlement phase in which about 10,000 autonomous swarm robots test infrastructure and risks before humans arrive. It argues this should complement, not replace, human settlement, and draws policy implications on AI governance, human oversight, accountability, planetary protection and space law.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes a robot-first preparatory phase using a ~10,000 autonomous robot swarm before human arrival on Mars.
Controlled failure by swarm systems can become operational learning that reduces settlement uncertainty.
Robot-first colonization should supplement, not replace, human settlement ambitions.
Policy implications stress AI governance, human oversight, accountability and planetary protection.
Calls for compliance with international space law.
